subject: Information Theory
title: Detection vs Correction
description: A quick, practical guide to Detection vs Correction.

hook.text: Detecting an error is easy. Fixing it without retransmission is hard. The difference defines two eras of coding.

buildup.text: Detection tells you something went wrong. Correction tells you exactly what went wrong and fixes it.

discovery.text: A code that detects d errors needs minimum distance d+1. Correcting t errors needs distance 2t+1.

twist.text: If you can retransmit (like TCP), detection is enough. If you can't (like space probes), correction is essential.

climax.text: Modern systems often combine both: correct small errors on the fly, detect large ones and request retransmission.

punchline.text: Detect to retry. Correct to continue. Choose wisely.

quiz.question: What minimum Hamming distance is needed to correct t errors?
